title: runtime-change-audit-shadow-evals-2025-06
body:
Summary:
This note captures the shadow-eval sweep we ran to assess three recent runtime/kernel changes landed on the staging branch: (A) Flash-attention microkernel swap (flash-v1 -> flash-v2), (B) Paged-KV memory-layout rewrite (layout-linear -> layout-interleaved), and (C) Continuous-batching scheduler adjustment (batch-window 12ms -> adaptive 8-20ms). The goal was to detect any subtle regressions in quality or correctness across our onboarding evaluation suites and to measure latency/throughput deltas under representative production mixes.

Key takeaways (short):
- flash-v2: median latency improved ~6–9% on short-context generation; however, a small but consistent drop (-0.9 pts) on the instruction-following micro-eval for long-context prompts (>=2048 tokens) likely due to kernel numeric ordering differences.
- paged-kv interleaved: memory throughput up ~12%, peak throughput improved for batched long-context workloads, but we observed 0.3% increased token-drop rate on checkpointed KV restore paths for some model sharding configs.
- continuous-batching adaptive: reduced p50 and p95 under mixed traffic (~8% p95 improvement) but introduced ordering jitter in multi-turn games (rarely shuffling turn metadata) — root cause traced to a race in request-to-cache-key mapping (race window widened by scheduler changes).

Methodology:
- Shadow-evals: For each change we exercised a shadow fleet of 100 GPU shards on staging with mirrored traffic (no live traffic impact). Each variant ran for 72 hours, seeded with 10M requests sampled from anonymized production traces (token-length distribution preserved).
- Eval suites: We used the standard onboarding eval packs plus two specialized prompt families created for this audit: fast-check (short imperative prompts, 1–64 tokens), long-horizon (multi-paragraph context, 1024–4096 tokens), multi-turn-dialog (context length 256–2048, turn metadata), and code-generation (prompt + test harness).
- Quality metrics: instruction-following score (0–100), hallucination-rate (manual labels over 500 samples), BLEU/ROUGE not used for broad instruction tests — we used model-assist accept-rate (human/heuristic combined) and logprob-stability delta.
- Telemetry collected: per-token latency (median/p95/p99), tail queue length, KV page fault rate, LRU eviction metric, cache-key collision count, and token-drop incidents.

Detailed results (aggregated):
1) Flash-attention swap (flash-v1 -> flash-v2)
- p50 latency: baseline 43ms -> 39.8ms (−7.4%)
- p95 latency: baseline 118ms -> 110ms (−6.8%)
- p99 latency: baseline 345ms -> 340ms (−1.4%)
- throughput (tokens/s per GPU): 12.2k -> 13.0k (+6.6%)
- instruction-following score (fast-check): 92.6 -> 92.9 (+0.3)
- instruction-following score (long-horizon): 88.1 -> 87.2 (−0.9)  <-- notable
- hallucination-rate (manual 500 samples, long-horizon): 7.4% -> 8.8% (+1.4pp)
- logprob-stability (mean delta of top-1 token logprob): -0.0015 -> -0.0031 (more variance)
Observations: numerical ordering in attention accumulation changed slightly producing marginal differences in long-context probability mass. Several long-horizon examples show truncation earlier than baseline in repeated-noun resolution tasks.
Action: add targeted regression tests for context-anchored tokens and run Kahan-sum style accumulation in the next flash-v2 patch.

2) Paged-KV memory-layout change (layout-linear -> layout-interleaved)
- average KV page read throughput: baseline 1.8GB/s -> 2.02GB/s (+12.2%)
- per-request median KV restore time (single-shot): 12ms -> 9.6ms (−20%)
- token-drop incidents (per 10k reqs): 0.09 -> 0.12 (+33%)  <-- small but visible
- checkpoint restore mismatches (investigated): 3 mismatches out of 12k checkpoint restores (baseline 1/12k)
- instruction-following score (paged-KV heavy long-horizon): 89.3 -> 88.9 (−0.4)
Observations: interleaved layout improves bandwidth and reduced cold-read latency. However, a subtle boundary alignment bug in the KV page assembler leads to occasional partial page writes during switchover under certain sharding offsets (affects only 0.01% of requests but visible in deterministic checksum tests).
Action: hotfix in page-assembler to validate page CRC and fallback to linear copy on mismatch; add unit tests for cross-shard boundary offsets.

3) Continuous-batching scheduler (fixed-window -> adaptive window 8-20ms)
- p50 latency: baseline 68ms -> 61ms (−10.3%)
- p95 latency: baseline 190ms -> 175ms (−7.9%)
- observed throughput (mixed traffic): +9% when many short requests present
- multi-turn dialog ordering jitter incidents: 0 -> 0.18 per 10k multi-turn sessions (traced to metadata routing)
- instruction-following score (multi-turn): 90.2 -> 89.9 (−0.3)
Observations: the adaptive scheduler reduces latency for short requests and better utilizes open slots, but the request ID->KV-key mapping race needs a short critical-section or stronger pinning per session.
Action: patch to enforce per-session pin mutex during batching window; re-run shadow test after patch.

Representative prompt diffs (long-horizon example):
-- prompt (truncated): 
"Context: The case file describes the timeline of events on 1989-12-20. The defendant contends that the witness misremembered the location. Question: Summarize the key disputes and identify factual anchors"
Baseline output (flash-v1/paged-linear): includes 4 factual anchors: dates, street names A/B, witness line items.
New output (flash-v2/paged-interleaved): produces same anchors but drops the second street name and merges two witness lines into one sentence (loss of one anchor).
Impact: downstream QA extractor missed an anchor; fail for structured extraction (we flagged in regression set).

Investigation notes (short):
- Reproduced deterministically by re-playing the same state with deterministic RNG seeds on both kernels. The difference is introduced during the attention accumulation (flash) step; when we force the old microkernel, outputs match.
- Paged-KV boundary bug reproduces on sharded restore when proportion of last-page writes modulo page-size != 0 and when background GC runs concurrently.
- Batching race manifests under high concurrency with interleaved multi-turn sessions; adding a short lock eliminates the ordering jitter but slightly increases p50 (~+1.5ms).

Recommendations and rollout plan:
1) Block rollout of flash-v2 to onboarding fleets until flash-v2.1 (Kahan accumulation) is merged and long-horizon regression pack passes. Target timeline: 3 business days.
2) Ship paged-kv page-assembler CRC fallback in next patch (PR referenced above) and gate interleaved layout behind a feature-flag for dedicated customer shards while we monitor real restore rates.
3) Apply batching scheduler patch (per-session pin) and re-run 48-hour shadow sweep; if stable, enable adaptive window on 50% of staging shards for an additional week before GA.
4) Add the following new deterministic tests to the onboarding harness: two long-horizon attention-anchored tests, three KV boundary restore tests with varied shard offsets, and a multi-turn ordering fuzz test.

Open items / TODOs:
- Diego: create PR for Kahan-sum accumulation on attention kernel (GH link in artifacts).
- Priya: extend long-horizon labeled set by +2k samples and re-run hallucination manual labeling after patches.
- Ethan: add CRC fallback and the unit tests for page-assembler; schedule a run against customer-sim workload.
- Ops: schedule a non-peak migration window for interleaved layout experimentation with canary tag.

Appendix: quick checklist for next run:
- [ ] Merge flash-v2.1 microkernel with Kahan patch
- [ ] Add KV CRC fallback + unit tests
- [ ] Add per-session pin to batching scheduler + run 48h shadow
- [ ] Expand long-horizon regression pack and re-label 2k samples
- [ ] Verify no new token-drop incidents in canary (threshold <0.05/10k)

Notes on reproducibility and data privacy:
- All shadow traffic used production sampling but was anonymized (PII scrubbed) before ingest.
- Deterministic reproductions were run with fixed RNG seeds and the same checkpoint artifacts used in production.
- We retained detailed traces for debugging; access limited to eng-applied-ml and SRE (link: GH actions artifact).

If you want a narrower slice of the raw telemetry or the per-prompt diffs in CSV, tell me which metric and I’ll export a filtered artifact (I have extracts for top-100 failing prompts).

Maya
eng-applied-ml
